key_insight: Travelling wall waves drive particle drift set by their intensity imbalance, but near-wall transport can reverse depending on fluid inertia and how the wall material moves.
engineering_relevance: Wave-driven cavity designs must account for wall kinematics and operating frequency to control particle transport direction reliably.
method: Decompose Lagrangian drift into Eulerian mean flow and Stokes drift.
Derive closed-form viscous-limit profiles and quadrature solutions at finite Womersley number.
Compare radial-only wall motion with motion that preserves local arc length to first order.
evidence_signal: Moving-domain simulations at azimuthal order m=2 and Wo²=10 recover the leading-order drift coefficients for both wall motions.
watch_item: Predictions are leading-order in wall amplitude; accuracy for larger deformations requires further validation.
paper_title: Lagrangian transport driven by travelling waves in a radially deforming circular cavity
